summary: Add visual and applied practice for pH titration curves, the chapter's clearest remaining learning gap.

improvements.where: note, after ## Method; request in pack diagrams and embed in note
improvements.why: Outcome 9701-7.2.9 requires learners to sketch pH titration curves, but the current note has no diagram and the figures gate fails.
improvements.what: Use graph_sketch to show pH against volume of alkali added for a strong acid–strong alkali and a weak acid–strong alkali titration, with clearly labelled starting pH, buffer region on the weak-acid curve, steep rise, and equivalence points at pH 7 and above pH 7 respectively. Distinguish the curves and explain in the note what their different shapes reveal.

improvements.why: The existing short questions are largely generic prompts; learners need to interpret curve features and indicator ranges in an exam-style setting.
improvements.what: Add one structured sketch-and-explain item for strong acid–weak alkali versus weak acid–strong alkali, requiring axes, direction, starting pH, equivalence pH and the weak-acid buffer region; add one data-based indicator-selection item that provides transition intervals and a curve's steep pH range, requiring a justified choice and rejection of an unsuitable indicator. Give specific mark points and explanations.
